dish: salmon-themed kaisendon and salmon goods in the food court
n: Michi-no-eki Salmon Park Chitose (道の駅 サーモンパーク千歳)
w: Chitose's salmon-river roadside station beside the Chitose Aquarium and its Indian water-wheel — a six-stall food court built around salmon.

dish: hokki (surf clam) salmon-don and hokki curry
n: Umi no Eki Platto Minato Ichiba, Tomakomai (海の駅 ぷらっとみなと市場)
w: Tomakomai port's market hall — Japan's top hokki-clam catch sold fresh, eaten in hokki-don and hokki curry at the stalls, with a small hokki museum.

dish: Date-musha bentō (Funka Bay scallop rice) and Date-milk white pudding
n: Michi-no-eki Date Rekishi no Mori (道の駅 だて歴史の杜)
w: Date's roadside station in its history park — Hansamu Shokudō, the scallop takikomi-gohan 'Date-musha' bento and Makiya's Date-milk pudding.

dish: 'torōri' cheese croquette and local-vegetable plates at Tōya-ko Shokudō
n: Michi-no-eki Tōya-ko (道の駅 とうや湖)
w: Hill-top roadside station above Lake Tōya with Mt Yōtei views; its shokudō and takeaway counter work the farm produce of the caldera rim.

dish: Rausu hokke and kinki (menme) set meals at Rausu no Umiaji Shiretoko Shokudō
n: Michi-no-eki Shiretoko-Rausu (道の駅 知床・らうす)
address: Hon-chō, Rausu, Menashi District, Hokkaido, Japan
w: The roadside station closest to Kunashir — its Shiretoko Shokudō is the local name for Rausu-landed hokke and kinki teishoku.

n: Kita no Kuni kara Jun no Banya, Rausu (北の国から 純の番屋)
address: Funami-chō, Rausu, Menashi District, Hokkaido, Japan
w: The fishermen's hut from the drama 'Kita no Kuni kara 2002 Yuigon', rebuilt as a diner serving Rausu-coast seafood.

dish: hanasaki-crab ramen at Restaurant Bird Pal
n: Michi-no-eki Swan 44 Nemuro (道の駅 スワン44ねむろ)
w: On Lake Fūren's swan shore — the Bird Pal dining room looks over the lagoon and is known for Nemuro's hanasaki-crab ramen.

dish: Ezo venison steak at Restaurant Tsuru
n: Michi-no-eki Akan Tanchō no Sato (道の駅 阿寒丹頂の里)
w: Akan's crane-country roadside station (with an onsen) — Restaurant Tsuru grills local Ezo-shika venison.

dish: raclette and dishes made with the farm's own cheese; nama-caramel
address: Moto-Satsunai Higashi 4-sen 311-6, Nakasatsunai, Kasai District, Hokkaido, Japan
w: Tanaka Yoshitaka's showcase ranch, birthplace of the nama-caramel boom — the café serves its own-cheese dishes and sweets.

dish: Tokachi junmai sake brewed on campus
n: Kamikawa Taisetsu Shuzō Hekiun-gura, Obihiro (上川大雪酒造 碧雲蔵)
address: Obihiro University of Agriculture and Veterinary Medicine campus, Obihiro, Hokkaido, Japan
w: Japan's first university-partnered sake brewery (2020), on the Obihiro agricultural university campus, brewing with Satsunai River water and Hokkaido rice.

dish: fresh bafun-uni don and Rishiri ramen
address: Oshidomari, Rishirifuji, Rishiri District, Hokkaido, Japan
w: Opposite Oshidomari ferry terminal — Rishiri's raw bafun-uni bowls (Apr-Oct) and kombu-broth Rishiri ramen.
The Wakkanai name for takoshabu — paper-thin mizudako from the Sōya Strait swished in broth, the city's signature dish.
Seasonal fishermen-direct uni-don shack by Cape Noshappu, made famous by touring riders.
